name: CA-32
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by fourteen points and Sherman is a long-serving incumbent
Challenger Thompson raised about $53,000 with under $1,000 cash on hand, with no outside spending
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Sherman's fourteen-point district lean, incumbency, and a roughly fifty-to-one fundraising advantage leave Thompson without a visible path, and prediction markets agree on a near-certain Democratic hold. Fundamentals point to a margin in the low twenties with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A large late infusion of outside spending against Sherman or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though it would likely still leave him heavily favored.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Sherman has represented this Los Angeles-area district for decades, and the seat leans Democratic by fourteen points on the partisan lean. He enters the general election with a dominant financial position: nearly $2.8 million raised and $2.6 million on hand, plus modest outside support. Republican Larry Thompson has raised about $53,000 and reported just $955 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls track the race and no expert raters have ranked it, but prediction markets put Sherman's chances near 96 percent. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and a large money gap — all point the same direction, making a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin the central expectation.
